title: Foldsmith+
summary: A papercraft design tool with 3D previews, folding instructions, and printable cutting sheets.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Foldsmith workshop with an editable papercraft model, assembly preview and export controls.
details: Choose from 61 designs, adjust dimensions and colors, and export a kit. The 3D model and cutting sheets come from the same geometry.
usage: Open a design, preview its assembly, and print at the indicated scale. The optional AI helper requires private access; the regular editor does not.
note: Digital geometry checks do not guarantee that every design will work with real materials.

title: Lanternfish LF-16
eyebrow: A computer small enough to inspect
summary: A 16-bit fantasy computer with its own language, compiler, emulator, IDE, and debugger.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Lanternfish IDE showing source code, a running cartridge, registers and machine state.
details: The LF-16 has 64 KiB of memory, a small pixel display, and four audio voices. Its included games and music tools run on the same machine you can program yourself.
usage: Run an included cartridge, then inspect or edit its source. Use breakpoints and stepping to follow execution. Best on desktop.

title: Signal Garden
eyebrow: Music you can read as a landscape
summary: A music composition tool where an editable landscape controls the score.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Signal Garden showing a luminous musical landscape alongside note beds and composition controls.
details: Notes, timing, and instruments shape a living garden. Built-in scenes and a random composer let you listen immediately; the editor lets you change individual parts and export WAV audio.
usage: Start the demo below, choose a scene, and press Play—or select Create random scene.

title: Parlour
summary: Two multiplayer party games: False Witness and Patent Pending.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Parlour’s hosted landing page introducing its host-screen and private-player party games.
details: False Witness mixes shared-scene memory with misleading witness reports. Patent Pending is a collaborative drawing and invention game with private constraints.
usage: Open a room on a shared host screen and have players join on their own devices. The hosted service may take a moment to wake up.

title: Tidal Archive
summary: A narrative game about saving a flooded city’s history when your archive holds only twelve pages.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Tidal Archive’s flooded city map, current scene, tide clock and narrative choices.
details: Explore Halloway before the relief boat leaves. Changing tides open routes, while conversations, recovered documents, and puzzles shape what you preserve and how the story ends.
usage: Open the game and begin a journey. Saves and portable journey files let you return later.

title: Event Horizon
eyebrow: A different clock. A different homecoming.
summary: An orbital flight game about black holes, time dilation, and delayed signals.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Event Horizon with an orbital map, black-hole optical view, mission brief, burn planner and clocks.
details: Across seven missions, plan burns, compare clocks aboard your ship and back home, and send messages that may arrive long after you expect. It combines spaceflight with a story shaped by elapsed time.
usage: Start the expedition and follow the early missions to learn the flight controls and planner.

title: Impossible Rooms
summary: A first-person exploration game with folded corridors, nested rooms, and impossible geometry.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: A first-person view inside Impossible Rooms, with richly lit architecture and connected doorways.
details: A closet can open into a cathedral, and a miniature house can contain itself. Find lanterns, follow your thread, and work out how the rooms connect.
usage: Explore a generated house, or use Architect mode to choose its ingredients. Rendering performance varies by device.

title: Worldseed
eyebrow: Change one assumption. Follow the difference.
summary: A procedural ecosystem you can rewind and branch into different histories.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Worldseed’s hexagonal atlas, species cards and timeline after advancing the simulation.
details: Watch a world develop, then change an event such as an ice age or a predator’s arrival. Compare species, traits, and regions across the resulting branches.
usage: Generate a world and explore its atlas, then fork its history. Best on desktop.
note: Uses simplified ecology and evolution rules.

title: Afterimage
summary: Explore one courtyard across four eras and change what survives into the present.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Afterimage’s brick courtyard in 2026, rendered as a first-person historical exploration scene.
details: Visit Chandler’s Court in 1926, 1958, 1991, and 2026. Your choices affect buildings, objects, and memories; a notebook keeps observations, testimony, and theories separate.
usage: Explore each era, collect evidence, and compare the histories your choices create.

title: Glyphcraft / Kettle Pass
eyebrow: Read a language. Make it your own.
summary: An invented-script puzzle and a workshop for designing your own writing system.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Glyphcraft’s Kettle Pass hut with a primer, handwritten script, a note and a tally stick.
details: Kettle Pass begins with unfamiliar writing in a mountain hut. Decipher the clues and compose a reply, then use the workshop to edit letters, word mappings, and grammar rules.
usage: Play the story or open the workshop. You can export a script bundle and a TrueType font.
note: Fonts use Private Use Area characters; they do not include a universal keyboard or shaping system.

title: Surveyor / Windbreak Ridge
eyebrow: A map someone else must trust
summary: A surveying game where a courier must navigate using the map you make.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Surveyor’s terrain diorama next to the player’s field sheet, survey pins and courier’s note.
details: Take bearings, identify landmarks, and draw a route. The courier follows your field sheet, then reports what happened so you can revise it. Later expeditions add transport constraints and ambiguous destinations.
usage: Begin with Windbreak Ridge to learn the survey tools. Best on desktop.

title: Automata
eyebrow: Draw the motion. Discover the machine.
summary: A mechanical sculpture workshop for designing motion with cams, linkages, and gears.
contribution: I directed and tested the project; GPT and Claude handled implementation and technical review.
imageAlt: Automata’s kinetic bird sculpture with visible cams, editable mechanism parts and motion timelines.
details: Edit a motion curve, dimensions, and timing, then watch a bird, cat, clock tower, or another sculpture move. Inspect the mechanism and export dimensioned SVG drawings.
usage: Start from a sculpture and adjust its motion or mechanism.
note: The model uses ideal rigid parts. Friction, strength, fit, and physical fabrication are not validated.
